advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the adoption floor so a signed event with a missing/non-int timestamp (ts==0) cannot set `_first_signed_ts` to 0 and disable the dormant-env suppression gate.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py:84-85: `ts = payload.get("timestamp")` then `ts = ts if isinstance(ts, int) else 0`
`if self._first_signed_ts is None or ts < self._first_signed_ts:` sets adopted to 0 when a signed event lacks a valid ts
findings(): `if not row.events or row.last_ts < adopted: continue` — with adopted==0 no env is suppressed by the gate
ABSENCE: no guard excludes ts==0 (or missing timestamp) signed events from setting the adoption floor
advisory.finding: A signed event whose `timestamp` is missing or non-int coerces to `ts = 0`, which then becomes `_first_signed_ts = 0`. Because the adoption gate skips an env only when `row.last_ts < adopted` (i.e. `< 0`, never true), a single malformed signed event defeats the false-positive guard entirely: every env with any event is then evaluated, so dormant pre-signing writers can be reported as UNSIGNED_ENV — the precise over-firing the gate exists to prevent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Only fold a signed event into `_first_signed_ts` when it has a usable (positive) timestamp, e.g. `if payload.get("author_sig") and ts > 0:` update the floor; or track a sentinel and treat ts==0 as unknown rather than earliest.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs fsck._scan over a fixture store with a post-adoption 0%-signed env and asserts an UNSIGNED_ENV line appears AND issue_count reflects it.
evidence: fsck.py line 108: `env_authorship.observe(filename, json.load(f))` — the new wiring
fsck.py lines 277-279: `env_findings = env_authorship.findings(); lines.extend(env_findings); issue_count += len(env_findings)`
ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_unsigned_env_fsck_heldout.py imports only EnvAuthorshipTally and _transform_json; no test calls fsck._scan, so the observe-hook and issue_count integration are untested
advisory.finding: The fsck._scan wiring for the new per-env check is not exercised by any test. Tests hit EnvAuthorshipTally.findings() and _transform_json separately, but nothing runs _scan to confirm that observe(filename, json.load(f)) is actually called on parsed payloads, that env_findings are appended to lines, and that issue_count += len(env_findings) runs. A regression that reverted the observe() hook to plain json.load(f), or dropped the issue_count increment, would pass the entire suite.
scenarios: A future edit reverts the Check-1 line to `json.load(f)` (dropping the observe hook) — findings() would always be empty in production but every unit test still passes
The `issue_count += len(env_findings)` line is removed — findings still print but stop being counted, silently defeating AC2 (COUNTED not advisory)
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an end-to-end test building a tiny tracker on disk (or a fake _ticket_dirs) with a signed env and an active unsigned env, call fsck._scan, and assert the returned lines contain the UNSIGNED_ENV line and issue_count is incremented by it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a _seam test with author_id set, signing_key unset, require_authenticated on, asserting the SKIP warning names the missing signing_key.
evidence: _seam.py lines 365-367: ternary selecting `"no resolvable identity (author_id) for this writer" if not author_id else "no identity.signing_key configured"`
test asserts `"author_id" in message` only for the no-identity case; the event dict `{"uuid": "ev-1"}` has no author_id, so only the first arm runs
ABSENCE: no test sets a resolvable author_id with signing_key unset (require_auth on) to exercise the 'no signing_key configured' message
advisory.finding: The 'no identity.signing_key configured' arm of the new two-branch warning message is untested. Only the `not author_id` arm ('no resolvable identity') is exercised. The else arm is reachable when author_id resolves but signing_key is falsy under require_authenticated=True; a regression swapping or breaking that branch's wording would go undetected.
scenarios: author_id resolves on a clone whose identity.signing_key is unset with require_authenticated on — the operator-facing message about WHICH input is missing is emitted here with no test pinning it
